reasons.urgency: Pressures you to act fast. Scammers rush you so you don't stop to check.
reasons.money_request: Asks you to send or pay money.
reasons.payment_rail: Mentions an instant or hard-to-reverse payment method (e.g. Pix, UPI, Zelle, gift cards, crypto).
reasons.new_number: Claims to be someone you know writing from a new or temporary number.
reasons.family_claim: Claims to be a family member without any way to verify it.
reasons.secrecy: Asks you to keep it secret. Real family and real banks don't do this.
reasons.avoid_voice: Avoids a voice call, so you can't recognise who it really is.
reasons.code_request: Asks you to share a verification/one-time code, which gives them access to your account.
reasons.credential_request: Asks for passwords, card details or other credentials.
reasons.account_threat: Threatens that an account or card is blocked or at risk.
reasons.safe_account: Asks you to move money to a 'safe account'. Banks never ask this.
reasons.remote_access: Asks you to install a screen-sharing or remote-access app.
reasons.refund_mistake: Claims money was sent by mistake and asks for it back.
reasons.prize: Says you won a prize or were 'selected'.
reasons.fee_to_unlock: Asks for a fee or deposit before you can receive something.
reasons.easy_income: Promises easy money for little work.
reasons.guaranteed_return: Promises guaranteed or unrealistically high returns.
reasons.authority: Claims to be a government, tax, toll or police authority.
reasons.delivery: Talks about a parcel or delivery.
reasons.bank_mention: Claims to be from a bank or its fraud team.
reasons.suspicious_link: The link looks suspicious (shortened, unusual domain or imitating a brand).
reasons.has_phone_number: Asks you to contact a phone number given in the message.
reasons.money_amount: Mentions a specific amount of money.

cautions.money: It asks you to send money. Even if it seems to come from someone you know, confirm by calling them on a number you already have before paying.
cautions.code: It asks for a code or password. Never share these, even with friends: a code is how accounts get taken over.
cautions.app: It asks you to install an app or share your screen. Don't, unless you started the conversation with a company you trust.

legit.label: Probably legitimate
next_steps: Stay careful: if the message asks for money or codes, confirm through a channel you already trust.

family_impersonation.label: Fake relative or friend
family_impersonation.description: Someone claims to be a family member or friend on a new number and asks for money urgently.
next_steps: Do not send money yet.
Call the person on the number you already have saved, or ask a question only they could answer.
If you can't reach them, check with another family member first.

fake_payment_receipt.label: Fake payment receipt / overpayment
fake_payment_receipt.description: Claims money was sent to you (often 'by mistake') and asks you to return it, usually with a forged receipt.
next_steps: Open your banking app directly and check your real balance. Ignore screenshots and receipts.
Do not 'refund' anything until the money is actually in your account and has cleared.
If a mistaken payment is real, your bank can reverse it; you don't need to send anything.

bank_impersonation.label: Fake bank agent
bank_impersonation.description: Pretends to be your bank's fraud team and pushes you to call a number, share codes or move money to a 'safe account'.
next_steps: Hang up or stop replying. Your bank will never ask you to move money to a 'safe account'.
Call your bank using the number on the back of your card or in the official app.
Never share one-time codes, PINs or passwords, and never install remote-access apps on request.

delivery_fee.label: Fake delivery / parcel fee
delivery_fee.description: Says a parcel is held and asks for a small fee or address confirmation through a link.
next_steps: Do not click the link or pay the fee.
Track parcels only through the courier's official app or the shop you ordered from.

toll_fine_tax.label: Fake fine, toll or tax notice
toll_fine_tax.description: Impersonates a government agency, toll operator or tax office demanding payment of an unpaid fine or refund claim.
next_steps: Do not pay through the link in the message.
Log in to the official government or toll website yourself (type the address) to check for real notices.

account_phishing.label: Account suspension / login phishing
account_phishing.description: Warns that an account (bank, streaming, email, social) is locked and asks you to 'verify' through a link.
next_steps: Do not click the link or enter your password.
Open the service's official app or website directly to check your account status.
If you already entered details, change your password now and turn on two-factor authentication.

verification_code_theft.label: Verification code theft
verification_code_theft.description: Asks you to forward a code that was 'sent by mistake'. This code lets them take over your WhatsApp, bank or email.
next_steps: Never share a verification or one-time code with anyone, even a friend.
If you already shared it, turn on two-step verification in the affected app immediately.

prize_lottery.label: Fake prize / giveaway
prize_lottery.description: Says you won a prize, lottery or giveaway and must pay a fee or share details to claim it.
next_steps: You can't win a contest you didn't enter. Real prizes never require a fee.
Do not pay, click or share personal details.

job_task.label: Fake job / task scam
job_task.description: Offers easy money for simple online tasks (liking videos, reviews), then asks you to deposit money to 'unlock' earnings.
next_steps: Legitimate employers never ask you to pay to work or to unlock wages.
Stop depositing money; earlier small 'payouts' are bait.

investment_crypto.label: Investment / crypto scam
investment_crypto.description: Promises guaranteed or unrealistically high returns, often in crypto or via a 'mentor' or trading group.
next_steps: Guaranteed high returns are a hallmark of fraud.
Check the firm with your country's financial regulator before investing anything.
